topic: Open session data extraction and S3 costs
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on the technical implementation for extracting open session data. Initially, it was noted that real-time functionality is no longer active due to changes in boxdatagrinder, and the current daily traffic growth suggests continued monitoring.

Regarding open sessions, [p1] suggested creating a service to periodically extract unclosed sessions from ClickHouse (CH) and send them elsewhere. The conversation confirmed that sending data every 5 seconds is unnecessary because chunks of data are flushed from the buffer every one to two minutes.

Separately, there was concern over a significant spike in S3 costs observed on May 31st. It was estimated that while the current cost ($30) is high for a short period, the total annual cost would be manageable (around $100).

[me] suggested an alternative approach to handling session data by mapping packed CSV files directly to tables, which might be slower but could bypass complex engine requirements like MergeTree.
decisions: A dedicated service will be created to periodically extract unclosed sessions from ClickHouse and send them out.
action_items: Someone needs to confirm if the external system actually utilizes the open session data being extracted.
